newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Milling wheat steady to lower in slow Budapest mkt.
newsitem.headline: Milling wheat steady to lower in slow Budapest mkt.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices eased for four maturities on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Monday as some market participants believed that improving weather could benefit the wheat that is yet to be harvested.
"Opinion about milling began to change," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.
He was referring to an earlier market consensus that this year's wheat crop, while significantly above last year's in volume terms, could be of lower quality due to persistent rains.
"If the weather forecasts prove correct, that could improve at least on the gluten content of the (as yet unharvested) wheat," Herczeg said.
Hot and dry weather is expected to return this week.
Hungary's wheat crop is expected to be around five million tonnes compared with last year's 3.9 million and some 30 percent of the crop awaits harvesting, which has been delayed by rains.
Milling wheat prices finished 20 to 400 forints per tonne lower for maturities from December to May while all other were unchanged.
Euro wheat, which started trading on Friday, rose by between 100 and 400 forints for maturities from September to December 1998 with only five open contracts.
Herczeg said euro wheat had serious trading potential but that it would take some time for trading to pick up.
Feed barley futures turned mixed in light volume as the market sought direction.

Maize futures rose by between 200 and 300 forints for maturities from December 1997 to July 1998 and Herczeg said prices were probably following higher international levels as domestic crop expectations were very good.
Total grains futures turnover was a below-average 644 lots or 375.2 million forints, down from Friday's modest 963 lots or 444 million forints.
